source: Derek, 2026-10-02: "do both, schema fix first." Round 2 (TC-R2) closed 2026-09-17 and is archived at _context/goal-tree-r2-closed.json. RECONCILIATION FINDING, recorded because it is the reason this round exists: TC-R2's M3-T1 shipped done honestly. All six of its criteria specify the GENERATOR and the DATA -- AC4 even walks the full forcing line -- and every one of them is satisfied. Not one criterion says the PLAYER is asked for the second move, so the multistep family was built, validated and shipped as a one-move puzzle. Its must_not and non_goals were both null. That is the gap R3-M1-AC5 exists to close, and it is why the release blockers here are interaction checks rather than data checks.

root.title: Tyranny Chess round 3: puzzles that actually take more than one move
root.notes:
Two sequenced tasks. M1 makes a multi-move puzzle playable as a multi-move puzzle; M2 uses the Lichess CC0 database's multi-move lines as a position source for harder ones. M1 gates M2: there is no point mining content a schema cannot represent.
[2026-10-03T02:04:55+00:00] Round 3 closed 2026-10-02. Zero criteria are human_confirmed: that is Derek's to claim.
non_goals: Regenerating the 27 existing multistep positions. Their continuations are backfilled from their own FEN; the positions themselves do not move.
Changing the tactical, restraint or survival records, whose puzzles are one-movers by construction.
Any change to the AI, the search, or evaluate(). Nothing here needs a variant-specific search change.
Importing any Lichess SOLUTION. Lichess supplies positions and a difficulty prior only.
Fixing the stale honest-limits count in the effort-router skill (flagged separately: 24 hook / 36 model over the last 60, against a claimed 60 / 1).
The two unread pc-coordination issues (#10, #11) addressed to this machine.
Publishing or pushing anything. Nothing leaves this machine without Derek saying so.
must_not: Ship a line field that the page never reads. This is the exact shape of the defect being fixed: TC-R2 validated the data, never the interaction, and the puzzle still ended after one move. A green data test is not evidence here.

Introduce a new banner comment above the GAME / UI banner in src/tyranny.html. tests/extract.js cuts the engine region at lastIndexOf of that banner prefix, so a new one silently SHRINKS the extracted engine while every suite still passes.

Insert code inside either range tests/extract.js slices (the engine region, and the second slice from the fen parser to runTests). Code landing there compiles into tests/engine.js and every suite fails.

Reuse the existing depth field for continuation length. On survival puzzles depth already means the survival horizon (all 153 shipped rows are depth 1), and overloading it is the drift this project has already been bitten by twice.
Reach the page by fetch(). The Artifact is a single file and file:// blocks fetch; data arrives as window.TYRANNY_PUZZLES or not at all.
Put the family predicates into the page. Judging and revealing must be O(1) lookups against stored data, not a browser-side re-derivation that can drift from tools/gen-puzzles.js.
Bump puzzles.json's schema without adding the new version to PUZ_SCHEMAS in src/tyranny.html. The page refuses an unknown schema outright, which takes puzzle mode offline.
Treat a Lichess line as forced. 51.4% of standard mate-in-1s are refuted by a self-capture, so a line that is best play in standard chess may be simply wrong in this game.

Edit puzzles/puzzles.json by any tool other than tools/gen-puzzles.js. A standalone backfill tool did exactly that during this round; the generator knew nothing about it, so a plain regeneration would have reverted the schema to 4 and dropped every line, and nothing would have failed until someone committed the result.

Judge input made while the opponent's scripted reply is still pending. A correct first move followed within half a second by any opponent-side click was scored 'Not it', counted a try and cancelled the stored reply.
Wait a fixed time for a timer that lives in the page. A sleep(900) for a 520 ms timeout passed on an idle machine and failed with every core busy, which is what a shared CI runner looks like.

children.title: A multi-move puzzle is played as a multi-move puzzle
Continuation representation, backfilled onto the 27 existing multistep records

criteria.evidence: tools/backfill-lines.js buildLine(); puzzles.json schema 5 carries line{plies,steps[]} on 27 records; field is optional so schema-4 puzzles keep their old one-move path
criteria.text: A puzzle may carry a line object holding plies and an ordered steps array, where a solver step carries an accept array of every move correct at that point and an opponent step carries the single reply it plays. The field is family-agnostic: any family may carry it.

criteria.evidence: diff vs HEAD across all 240 records: 0 pre-existing fields changed (fen, solutions, decoys, counts, rationale, source all identical), exactly 1 key added (line); step-0 accept == solutionsUci for all 27
criteria.text: All 27 existing multistep records gain a line whose step 0 accept-set equals their existing solutions, derived from each record's own fen, with the 27 positions and their FENs byte-identical to the shipped file.

criteria.evidence: fewest-mating-answers then UCI tie-break; mutation-proven on mul-0017 (26 replies): swapping in a non-chosen reply is rejected with 'line stored a reply with 2 mating answers; the fewest available is 1', and the unmutated record validates clean as a control
criteria.text: The stored opponent reply is the one with the FEWEST mating answers, tie-broken by UCI string, so the same input reproduces a byte-identical puzzles.json.

criteria.evidence: tests/puzzles.js re-derives every line from FEN alone; forcingLine proves all L.count replies have a mating answer, not just the stored one; 303 passed 0 failed with 9 line mutations all caught
criteria.text: tests/puzzles.js re-derives every line from the puzzle's FEN alone and additionally asserts that EVERY opponent reply -- not just the stored one -- still has a mating answer, so fixing one reply is proven not to be a loss of generality rather than assumed.

criteria.evidence: tests/browser.js real headless Chrome: correct move 1 -> state 'mid' not 'solved', solved-set empty, Next disabled; stored reply a7b7 lands; wrong move 2 -> 'wrong'; Try again restores the ORIGINAL fen and step 0; full line -> 'solved' with real checkmate on the board. 141 passed, 0 failed
criteria.text: A headless interaction test drives puzJudge: given a multistep puzzle, the correct first move leaves the puzzle NOT solved, the stored reply is applied to the board, the mating second move marks it solved, and a legal non-mating second move marks it wrong and offers Try again. This is the criterion TC-R2's M3-T1 was missing.

criteria.evidence: sha256 tests/engine.js = 23cf16583cdbf5f58c4194345abdc81fc382c7682084486c033dee5d2f78718f before and after; engine slice still ends at line 901, second slice moved 1572-1590 -> 1711-1729 (shifted below my inserts, not into them)
criteria.text: The extracted tests/engine.js is byte-identical before and after the src/tyranny.html edits, proving no inserted code landed in either range tests/extract.js slices and no banner shrank the engine region.

criteria.evidence: puzzles.json schema 5; PUZ_SCHEMAS = [2,3,4,5]; 'index.html matches src/tyranny.html + puzzles/puzzles.json'. The stale-inline guard fired first and refused the build until --inline was re-run
criteria.text: puzzles.json carries schema 5, src/tyranny.html's PUZ_SCHEMAS accepts it, and build.js --check reports no drift between src, puzzles.json and index.html.

criteria.evidence: Reveal mid-line prints 'R(x)h2 ... R(x)b7 (one of 26, all losing) ... Rxh6#'; Next stays disabled at 'mid'; Try again resets step to 0 and restores the puzzle fen byte-for-byte
criteria.text: Reveal and Try again both behave correctly mid-line: Reveal names the whole remaining line, Try again restores the ORIGINAL puzzle position and resets the step counter to 0, and Next stays disabled until the line is finished.

criteria.evidence: All suites pass at the close. node tests/run-all.js exit 0: 27/8/24/13/396/26 = 494 checks (last commit bb6ea9f measured 388 = 27/8/24/13/290/26). node tests/browser.js: 166 passed 0 failed (last commit measured 114). In-page suite 48/0. No suite has fewer assertion call sites than HEAD (puzzles.js 54 to 135, browser.js 141 to 199, the rest equal). Lines removed vs HEAD: three, each replaced by a stronger or generalized assertion (two schema-4 pins, one hard-coded 240/240).
criteria.text: The full suite passes with no test deleted or weakened, and its check count is reported before and after.

The generator is the single writer of puzzles.json: regenerating with the committed parameters (500 games, seed 20260914, target 20, pinned --now) reproduces the committed file BYTE FOR BYTE, so the schema bump and every line survive a regeneration. A cheaper standing check in tests/puzzles.js compares the generator's record construction against every committed sweep record and its SCHEMA constant against the file.
criteria.evidence: Full regeneration reproduces the committed file BYTE-IDENTICALLY, twice. First the pre-seed schema-5 file (--multistep none): sha256 b96c51ae8c13de8a4da7281243d6a313e291eb3274534bf1a14dd2156897ea56, 287433 bytes. Then the FINAL 280-puzzle file, in an independent second run with the committed generatedAt 2026-10-03T01:47:33Z: sha256 64fce79d6656dcb943436c4c5939eab347c1bd2ecca4a9bff299523267a303c4, 363064 bytes. Standing checks in tests/puzzles.js: all 87 sweep records rebuild identically through buildEntry, the schema constant equals the file, and a stale seed fails before the sweep starts.

criteria.text: An early click inside the opponent's reply window is ignored, not judged: after the correct first move, an opponent-side move made in the same page turn leaves the puzzle in 'mid', counts no try, adds nothing to the board, and the stored reply still lands. Tested with both clicks inside ONE page evaluation so the timer cannot fire between them.
criteria.evidence: puzJudge now refuses input while the opponent step is pending. Live repro before the fix (mls-0012, correct move then any Black move at once): state wrong, tries 1, stored reply never landed. Regression test in tests/browser.js, both clicks inside ONE page evaluation so the timer cannot fire between them: state stays mid, tries unchanged, board unchanged, stored reply e8f6 still lands. Reveal inside the window, leaving puzzle mode inside the window and re-entering were also exercised on a live page: no stale reply, no page errors.

criteria.text: The browser suite waits for the page's own timers by polling, not by sleeping, and passes with every core saturated (12 busy loops on 8 cores), the condition under which the fixed-sleep version failed.
criteria.evidence: Fixed sleeps replaced by polling until(). Before: 12 busy loops on 8 cores made the suite fail one check (the reply landed on the board, got 2 want 3). After: two runs under the same load, 166 passed 0 failed each, plus six normal runs at 166/0.

children.title: Harder puzzles mined from the Lichess CC0 multi-move lines
non_goals: Any claim that Stockfish scores Tyranny positions. Measured this session and false: Stockfish assumes NEITHER side can self-capture, so it over-rates the attacker. tac-0003 is Qe6 mate to Stockfish and no mate at all in Tyranny, because Black answers king-takes-own-pawn on g7.

children.title: Mine multi-move lines for genuine multi-step Tyranny puzzles

criteria.evidence: Measured, plain counts, recorded in puzzles/multistep-seed.json and the README: 200000 of 6157341 rows (3.25 percent), 7 shards in 1145 s; 1125354 positions tested; 234 passed the multistep predicate; 167 rejected for fewer than 2 opponent replies; 67 kept (one per row); the first 40 in scan order ship. Yield per 20000-row block ranged 4 to 12 (mean 6.7); the earlier 20000-row probe projected about twice the real figure. The projection to the whole file (9 to 10 hours) is labelled as extrapolation and was not run.
criteria.text: The yield of multi-solver-move Lichess rows that survive as Tyranny multi-step puzzles is MEASURED and recorded as a plain count over a stated number of rows scanned, before any claim about how many such puzzles are achievable. This is currently unmeasured and must not be assumed.

criteria.evidence: No Lichess move is used as an answer. The miner selects positions with tryMultistep, the generator predicate. gen-puzzles.js deriveMultistepSeeds recomputes solution, line, decoys and difficulty from each FEN and THROWS on disagreement (three throw tests). tests/puzzles.js re-derives all 280 puzzles independently: 280 of 280 verified sound. The only Lichess fields stored are source metadata.
criteria.text: Every stored line is re-derived by the local predicate against Tyranny rules. The Lichess Moves column selects candidate positions and nothing else; no imported move is ever trusted as an answer.

criteria.evidence: All 40 seeded puzzles carry source with db, id, rating, popularity, themes, url and ply. The validator rejects a missing source, a wrong database, a non-lichess link, a negative ply, a non-numeric rating and a missing id (six mutants, all rejected).
criteria.text: Each mined puzzle carries its source id, rating and game URL, as the existing survival records already do, so a reader can trace it to a real game.

criteria.evidence: No shortfall to report: 67 candidates against a cap of 40. The predicate was not loosened: tryMultistep, matesIn2 and isMate are byte-identical to HEAD bb6ea9f (checked by extracting each function from HEAD and from the working tree and comparing). The two-reply filter is a recorded selection setting in the seed, not a change to the predicate.
criteria.text: If the yield proves too low to reach a useful count, the shortfall is reported as a count and the predicate is NOT quietly loosened.

criteria.evidence: Deeper lines play through the unchanged page code. tests/browser.js builds a synthetic FIVE-ply line from the opening position and plays it in real headless Chrome: move 1 leaves it open, the scripted reply lands, a wrong move mid-line is judged wrong, Try again restores the original FEN and step 0, move 2 leaves it open, solved only after the third move. The generator and validator build three-ply lines on purpose, since the family is mate in two.
criteria.text: Puzzles deeper than the existing two-ply multistep family are playable through the same R3-M1 line representation with no second schema change.

The Lichess seed is reproducible and traceable: puzzles/multistep-seed.json records the database file's byte size and SHA-256, the rows scanned, the shard count and every filter, and tests/puzzles.js asserts the committed puzzles equal what the generator derives from that seed, in order.
criteria.evidence: Seed provenance recorded: dbFile bytes 307234795 and sha256 76335bfa7d7c4a7f93c1366d81549e53951ebb79dd43d34904cab8f22d962f8d, rowsScanned 200000, shards 7, minReplies 2, perRow 1. The DB file was re-hashed after the scan and equals the seed. tests/puzzles.js asserts the 40 seeded puzzles equal what the generator derives from the seed, in order. Stated limit, documented in the README and the miner header: the hash is of the file named by --db at merge time and the shards do not verify it; a fingerprint of the rows actually read would close that and has not been built.

criteria.text: Nothing shipped claims more than was measured: the README says source.rating is the rating of the STANDARD puzzle the position came from and not the difficulty of this one, that opponent-reply breadth as a difficulty axis is a design choice and not a measurement, and that the yield came from a prefix of the database with any extrapolation labelled as one.
criteria.evidence: The README says source.rating is the rating of the standard puzzle and not of this one, that requiring two replies is a design choice and not a measured effect on difficulty (32 of the 40 give exactly two), that the yield comes from a 3.25 percent prefix with the projection labelled and not run, and that the page never shows the source link.

criteria.text: Seeded puzzle ids are built from the Lichess puzzle id and the ply, so they cannot move when the seed is re-mined; asserted as a property (same positions in either order get the same ids). An explicit --multistep or --survival path that does not exist is an error raised before the sweep, not a silent skip.
criteria.evidence: Seeded ids are mls-lichessid-ply, for example mls-002mG-1. Property test: the same positions get the same ids in either order of the seed. A missing ply and a duplicate id each throw. An explicit --multistep or --survival path that does not exist now exits non-zero with does not exist, before the sweep starts (four checks across the two flags). The 40 seeded records are otherwise identical to the previous version apart from the id (40 of 40).

children.title: README matches the shipped state, enforced by a test

criteria.text: Every puzzle count the README states -- the headline total and each row of the family table -- equals the count in puzzles/puzzles.json, enforced by a test that fails when they differ rather than checked by eye.
criteria.evidence: tests/puzzles.js compares every count the README states to the data: headline total, Puzzles-section total, number of families, and each family row (280 total; 20 tactical, 40 restraint, 67 multistep, 153 survival). The same rules are shown six deliberately wrong READMEs and reject all six: headline off by one, section total off by one, stale multistep row, wrong number of families, mention of the retired backfill tool, family table removed.

criteria.text: The README documents schema 5, the line field, the Lichess multistep seed and how to regenerate it, naming tools/line.js and tools/lichess-multistep.js, and does not mention the retired standalone backfill tool.
criteria.evidence: The README documents schema 5, the line field, both seeds and how to regenerate them, tools/line.js and tools/lichess-multistep.js, the one-writer rule, and the early-click and flakiness history. grep for backfill-lines finds nothing, and a test enforces that.

criteria.text: The README's honest-limits section states what this round did NOT establish: that Stockfish cannot score Tyranny positions (measured: it assumes neither side can self-capture, so it over-rates the attacker), and the three limits named in R3-M2-AC7.

criteria.text: The check counts the README quotes match the actual output of node tests/run-all.js and node tests/browser.js at the close.
criteria.evidence: The README quotes 494 checks (27/8/24/13/396/26) and 166 browser checks, printed by node tests/run-all.js (exit 0) and node tests/browser.js (exit 0) on 2026-10-02. The baseline was measured, not recalled: a clean copy of HEAD bb6ea9f ran 388 and 114.

criteria.text: No scratch this round created is left behind unexplained: the one-off diagnostic scripts and the point-in-time hash file are removed once their findings are recorded, and the instrument that is kept (sf-probe.py) states in its header what it measured and what it cannot.
criteria.evidence: Removed five untracked scratch files: qe6.js, sf-why.py, sf-disagree.py, engine-before.sha and multistep-probe-20k.json (their findings are in sf-probe.py, the README and this tree). git status now shows exactly 8 modified and 5 new files, all intended. criteria.evidence: grep for over-rate in README.md and _context/sf-probe.py finds only the withdrawal note. Both now say a standard engine names mating moves the variant refutes (tac-0003: a wrong move, not a wrong verdict) and that whether it misjudges who is winning was not measured.
